features.title: Native Settings shell, ported
features.summary: The sidebar Settings trigger, connection recovery pill, Desktop update indicator, section navigation, General section, onboarding coordinator and Mod+, shortcut of the native Settings shell, served by this bundle with the native row switched off.
failureModes: When the running DSH ships another version of the native Settings package, the Host warns at boot and General shows the running version, so the port is refreshed instead of drifting silently.

The native welcome notice stores its acknowledgement in the switched-off row's namespace, so the shell ports that step and keeps the acknowledgement in its own namespace; someone who acknowledged the native notice sees it once more.

verification.testName: matches the native Settings package this workspace builds against

telemetry.reason: Client-only: Native Settings shell, ported renders browser state and starts no Host work of its own.

features.title: DSH release notice and TL;DR
features.summary: The Settings trigger marks a new public DSH release, and General compares it with the installed Host version, shows a concise English TL;DR across newer releases, links to the official notes, and lets the user dismiss that release notice.
failureModes: GitHub is unavailable or returns an invalid payload; Settings stays usable and offers a manual retry.
The installed version is absent from the bounded release history; the plugin reports that comparison is unknown instead of guessing.
Release notes are bounded and rendered as escaped plain text; malformed or HTML content cannot inject client markup.

externalDependencies.boundary: Host-only GET to the fixed public deepseek-harness releases endpoint; response data is schema-validated, bounded, and rendered as untrusted text.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: release-status.test.ts injects a fixed fetch response and covers release ordering, version matching, English note extraction, redirects, and malformed payloads.

verification.testName: lists releases after the installed version and keeps their links on GitHub

telemetry.testName: records a dsh release check span with whether an update exists

features.title: Settings in the side panel
features.summary: The thread's right side panel offers Settings beside the other panel cards: picking that card opens a Settings tab in the panel, which lists every section and plugin page and drills into one on a narrow panel (a wide one keeps the dialog's two columns). The gear, the palette and Mod+, can also send Settings there.
reach: click text "Edit Settings in this panel."
failureModes: Without a thread on screen there is no side panel to open Settings in, so the guide card and the palette action do nothing.
The guide hides entry descriptions once it lists many entries; the catalog reach and its journey find the card by that description, so a crowded guide changes that path.

drills into a side-panel section and goes back to the section list

telemetry.reason: Client-only: Settings in the side panel renders browser state and starts no Host work of its own.

features.title: Search section controls and open them at the control
features.summary: Controls that live Settings sections publish as search entries (dshx settings.section metadata.searchEntries) are found while their sections stay unmounted, listed under their section; picking one opens that section with target set to the entry id, and the section scrolls to and focuses it. General publishes its coding-view switch. The read-only settings_list tool searches the same entries for the Agent.
reach: fill combobox "Search the command palette" "Settings: General"
failureModes: A section whose published entries do not decode is skipped with one console warning.
A section registered imperatively must publish its own entries with publishSettingsSearchEntries.
